item.title: RTT: Ref. 6286_All. 2 - Study of thermodynamic and mass transport phenomena for material characterization and process performance analysis (Univ. BOLOGNA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-03 23:59
Institution: Univ. BOLOGNA, Bologna
Field: Industrial and information engineering / 09/ICHI-01 Sistemi, metodi e tecnologie dell'ingegneria chimica e di processo

The successful candidate will conduct research on chemical engineering principles, with a primary focus on mass transport phenomena in solid, polymeric, and composite materials. The objective will be to evaluate their suitability for a wide range of process engineering applications, including membrane-based separations, bioseparation processes, and barrier technologies. Research activities will involve sample preparation, morphological and structural characterization, physicochemical and functional analysis, and the experimental determination of transport properties and model parameters required for the quantitative description of the mechanisms governing material and process performance.…

item.title: RTT: Cross-Layer Solutions for Wi-Fi and Bluetooth Networks: Cross-Link CSI Prediction, MAC Scheduling, and Physical-Layer Privacy Protection in Wi-Fi Sensing 2026_RTT_DEIB_7 (Politecnico MILANO)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-03 12:00
Institution: Politecnico MILANO, Milano
Field: Industrial and information engineering / 09/IINF-03 Telecomunicazioni

The research will focus on wireless and Internet of Things networks based on Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, integrating communication and Wi-Fi sensing through cross-layer solutions spanning the physical layer and medium access control (MAC) protocols. Channel State Information (CSI) and cross-link channel prediction will be used to optimize transmission scheduling and radio resource allocation, reducing CSI acquisition overhead. Physical-layer security and privacy threats will be analyzed, and countermeasures against unauthorized sensing will be developed, including CSI obfuscation and randomized beamforming, while limiting the impact on legitimate communications.
